clue.text: Leading figure accepted support with hesitation

parts.note: standard as an adjective means normal, generally accepted
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: A prominent person agrees, a little falteringly, to give their backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carries the flag at the head of an army, and figuratively is the foremost champion of a cause.

clue.text: Rubbish, tons ready

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
fruit that is ripe is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Heaps of waste are piled up awaiting collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow stomach lining, and colloquially any worthless nonsense or drivel.

clue.text: Number above thousand in assembly as a rule

indicators.note: in a down entry, being above means written earlier in the column

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: in places the preceding item inside the word that follows it

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering of people
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: The headcount at a meeting of a thousand-strong crowd is, typically, high.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts the first piece on top, so it comes first; the thousand then sits inside the gathering word.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and as a rule are both adverbs meaning usually, in the ordinary course of events.

clue.text: Hopes to have endless jelly and food

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: rations are allotted portions of food

explanation.surface: Someone's dreams amount to an unlimited supply of jelly and snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirations are ambitions or wishes, so the plural noun matches the noun reading of hopes.

clue.text: Swindle involving upper-class pair

indicators.note: to involve is to include or wrap in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A con trick carried out by two posh fraudsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a twosome, especially two performers working together.

clue.text: Use line in poem strangely unknown

indicators.note: done in an odd, unusual way, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: Advice to a poet: include an odd, obscure line in your verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The line letter goes into the poem's letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make use of it, so both are verbs for putting a thing to work.

clue.text: Control, say, put back

parts.note: to rein in is to control

explanation.surface: Instructions to restore authority by announcing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position.

clue.text: Court star with degree of error, sadly losing love

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong or upset, so the letters are disturbed into a fresh order
losing means giving something up, so that item is taken out of the letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A tennis star making a few mistakes loses a game to love.
explanation.walkthrough: One O is removed from the phrase, then the rest is rearranged. Roger Federer is the Swiss tennis champion with twenty Grand Slam titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Federer is one of the greatest tennis players, and tennis is played on a court.

clue.text: Complain about deceiver

indicators.note: about as in turning about, facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rail against something is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a person who deceived them.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar is a person who tells untruths, which is a kind of deceiver.

clue.text: Expert politician can start to gain encouragement

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

explanation.surface: A skilled MP can begin to win support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the container noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompting is urging or nudging someone to act, a form of encouragement.

clue.text: Opening remark about church and people

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped around the later ones

explanation.surface: An introductory word on the church and its congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The church and people letters go inside the remark word, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement is a beginning or start, just as an opening is.

clue.text: Outdoor work English rain ruined

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An outdoor English performance spoilt by the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Track bearing north and south and back

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the track word carries the compass points inside it

parts.note: spoor is the track of an animal

explanation.surface: Directions for a route running north to south and then returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction to go back, but it is the definition in its sense of supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor a person or project is to back it, usually with money.

clue.text: Sins in tales designed to produce piety

indicators.note: designed means planned or arranged, so the phrase's letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Morality tales feature wrongdoing to teach virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintliness is holiness of life, the quality of being devout and good.

clue.text: Inflexible doctor with refusal left one suffering itch

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so its letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A rigid doctor won't treat the patient, leaving someone itching.
explanation.definitionFit: Monolithic means massive, uniform and rigid, like a single block of stone, hence unbending.

clue.text: Family upset before I praise a racing driver

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, which in a down entry turns the word upside down

explanation.surface: Relatives are distressed before someone acclaims a motor-racing hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the family word upside down. Niki Lauda was the Austrian Formula One world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauda won three Formula One world championships, so he is a famous racing driver.

clue.text: Mug following wizard

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following
an ace or wizard is an expert

explanation.surface: A dupe trailing after a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is slang for the face, not a cup or a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is informal British slang for a person's face.

clue.text: Processed meat finished on drive over island

parts.note: something past is over and done
to ram is to drive in by force

explanation.surface: A cured meat is eaten up on a road trip across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked beef, a cured deli meat.

clue.text: Going westward in trek under attack

indicators.note: west is leftwards on a map, so in an across entry the letters run right to left
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Travellers heading west on a hike come under assault.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue westward means right to left, so the hidden run is read backwards. 'under attack' looks like one phrase, but 'under' lends letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuke is to strike with nuclear weapons, a drastic form of attack.

clue.text: Break from working not possessed by fearful energy

indicators.note: something possessed by another is held within it, so it goes inside
working as in being worked or kneaded, so the following word's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Taking leave from a job because of nervous exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like the job you take a break from; here it is the signal to rearrange the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a rule or law is to break or violate it.

clue.text: Elevated biography covering time with depth

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the biography word encloses what follows

parts.note: a life is a written biography

explanation.surface: A lofty life story that spans its era with profundity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifted means raised up to a higher position, the same as elevated.

clue.text: Cakes made with rice as arranged, about fifty

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the number
arranged means put in order, here a new order for the letters before it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A recipe for about fifty rice cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long choux pastries filled with cream and topped with chocolate, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Strong batting, perfect?

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is in
the perfect is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is a powerful innings flawless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' reads as flawless, but the question mark signals the grammar sense: the perfect is an example of a tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme in strength or degree, as with intense heat or feeling.

clue.text: Courage never wavering

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady and shifting, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Bravery that never falters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or daring, the steadiness to face danger.

clue.text: Just qualified after event's leader gave up

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: to quit is to give up

explanation.surface: A competent competitor withdraws once the race front-runner retires.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, which is what just means as an adjective.

clue.text: Shout of disapproval from oaf, right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a boor is a rude oaf

explanation.surface: A lout is jeered and sent packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo is the noise an audience makes to show contempt or disapproval.

clue.text: Gold used by artist to create atmosphere

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A painter uses gold leaf to give a picture mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive feeling or air surrounding a place or person.

clue.text: Moving dirt, spared poor burrowing arachnid

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Shifting earth, a creature digging in spares a weak victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor spider digs a burrow sealed with a hinged lid, from which it ambushes prey.
